relationships.title: Unattributed non-marketable equity securities (private stakes), carrying value at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Up to {funded} of Nvidia's private stakes match no sized deal; OpenAI and other named stakes of unknown cost sit inside it.
relationships.definition: Nvidia's private company stakes, carried at cost less impairment and adjusted for observable price changes, totalled the disclosed amount at 2026-10-25. This record is what remains after subtracting the named private stakes whose amounts are disclosed. It is the part of Nvidia's private portfolio that no named relationship explains, and it is an upper bound because several named stakes, including OpenAI, have no disclosed funded amount.

funded.label: analysis
funded.note: Analysis. Aggregate at carrying value; named items at cost, the only available proxy. Upper bound: OpenAI and other named private stakes are not quantified and are not subtracted.

components.note: Disclosed: non-marketable equity securities, carrying value at 2026-10-25
Less Nscale Series B preferred, cost (rel_nscale_eq_2025)
Less Nscale SAFE converted to Series C-3, cost (rel_nscale_eq_2025)
Less Nscale Series C-4 preferred, cost (rel_nscale_eq_2025)
Less SB Energy prepaid forward, amount funded 2026-08-17 (rel_sb_energy_eq_2026)

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Private equity stakes lose value with the AI funding cycle, but Nvidia's exposure is capped at carrying value and does not grow as the issuers weaken.
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: Private AI companies raise later rounds at lower prices
first_order.mechanism: Unattributed private stakes are marked down through impairments in Other income, net
first_order.text: Private stakes Nvidia does not name are written down when their prices fall, as the $1.8 billion impairment in the quarter to 25 October 2026 shows.

second_order.trigger: Investees inside the Unattributed remainder also buy Nvidia systems
second_order.mechanism: Unattributed equity may fund purchases of Nvidia products that cannot be traced to a named counterparty
second_order.text: Because Nvidia does not name these private investees, no reader can test whether the money returns to Nvidia as purchases of its systems.

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified (not subtracted): OpenAI Series C preferred (rel_openai_eq_2026; $30B committed in a round closed 2026-03-31, funded amount not disclosed); Anthropic Series G portion of the November 2025 agreement (rel_anthropic_eqc_2025, amount not disclosed); Mistral, Safe Superintelligence, Thinking Machines, Reflection, Cohere, Sakana, Point2, Figure, Wayve, Skild AI, Black Forest Labs, Scale AI, Anysphere, Databricks, Commonwealth Fusion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum, TerraPower, Lambda, Crusoe (three rounds), Firmus (three), Together AI (three). Analysis: if the OpenAI $30B had been fully paid by 2026-10-25, the remainder would fall to about $29.0B. Excluded: Anthropic IPO placement (closed 2026-11-20, after the date, and a public stake); Nscale convertible notes (debt, not equity); equity method LP interests (Helix, Brookfield) which sit in the Non-marketable securities line of $65,528M (ev_130015) but outside the $61,650M equity table. SB Energy prepaid forward ($1.5B funded 2026-08-17, settles into non-voting Class N shares): its classification inside this line is analysis. Basis check after the critic review: every subtraction is a cost stated by a source for a private stake (Nscale Series B, SAFE and Series C-4 prices; SB Energy prepaid amount). Cost versus carrying value: the aggregate includes cumulative gross unrealized gains of $9.9B (ev_130021) and losses and impairments of $2.2B (ev_130022).

relationships.title: Unattributed publicly held equity securities at 2026-10-25: not computable against 13F values at 2026-09-30
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia's listed holdings cannot be matched to its balance sheet line by line, because the dates and instruments differ, so no unattributed figure is shown.
relationships.definition: Nvidia's stakes in listed companies, measured at fair value, totalled the disclosed Level 1 and Level 2 amounts at 25 October 2026. Level 2 holds unregistered warrants and preferred stock convertible into common stock, which Nvidia's holdings report (Form 13F) does not list, and that report is dated 30 September 2026. Because the dates and the instruments differ, no unattributed remainder is computed; two bridge rows compare listed shares and Level 2 instruments separately.

funded.note: Not computable: see the two bridge rows.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Public stakes fall with AI equity prices, and Nvidia's exposure is capped at fair value; it does not grow as issuers weaken.
credit.notes: Analysis. No remainder is computed: the 13F values are 25 days earlier than the balance sheet date and exclude Level 2 instruments; see bridge_rows. Excluded from every total.

first_order.mechanism: Named and unnamed public stakes are marked to market through Other income, net
first_order.text: Nvidia's holdings report names Intel, SpaceX and CoreWeave as its largest listed positions, so a fall in its public equity value can be traced mainly to those names.

second_order.trigger: Lock-ups on Unattributed and named public stakes expire
second_order.mechanism: Sales of locked positions could weigh on the issuers' share prices
second_order.text: Nvidia held $21.0 billion of listed equity under short-term lock-up at 25 October 2026, so when those lock-ups end, sales by Nvidia could move the prices of companies it backs (analysis).

relationships.notes: Not computable; grounded figures kept here. Disclosed at 2026-10-25: publicly held equity securities Level 1, fair value $38,372 million (ev_130011); Level 2 (unregistered warrants, convertible preferred), fair value $10,516 million (ev_130012). Named common stock in Nvidia's 13F at 2026-09-30, reported values: Intel $19,366,947,532 (ev_50021), SpaceX Class A $19,683,145,466 (ev_50031), CoreWeave $4,113,227,313 (ev_50019), Coherent $2,241,510,617 (ev_50027), Synopsys $1,893,762,250 (ev_50023), Nokia ADS $738,797,875 (ev_50025), Nebius Class A $280,809,479 (ev_50015), Generate Biomedicines $12,516,542 (ev_50029); total $48,330,717,074, which exceeds Level 1 by about $10 billion at a date 25 days earlier. Named Level 2 instruments in the register at cost, not fair value: Marvell convertible preferred $2.0 billion (ev_60052, rel_marvell_eq_2026), Lumentum convertible preferred $2.0 billion (ev_60066, rel_lumentum_eq_2026), Nebius pre-funded warrant $2.0 billion (ev_40057, rel_nebius_eq_2026), Corning warrants $0.5 billion (ev_60088, rel_corning_eq_2026); total $6.5 billion. IREN investment rights (rel_iren_eq_2026) carry no value. Nvidia's table does not say in which level the SpaceX shares sit. Excluded: debt convertible into a public company's equity, $3,471 million (ev_50098), which sits in marketable debt securities. Anthropic (public from 2026-11-20) is after the date. The earlier remainder of $557.3 million (Level 1 plus Level 2 less the eight 13F values) was withdrawn after critic round 3 because it subtracted common stock values from a total that includes Level 2 instruments.

bridge_rows.note: Not comparable. Nvidia's holdings report of 30 September 2026 shows $48.3 billion of named common stock, $10 billion more than Level 1 at 25 October 2026; the dates differ and Nvidia does not say in which level the SpaceX shares sit.

Marvell and Lumentum convertible preferred ($2 billion each), the Nebius pre-funded warrant ($2 billion) and the Corning warrants ($500 million), at cost, not fair value. IREN's investment rights carry no value.

relationships.title: Unattributed guarantees: maximum gross exposure not tied to a named counterparty at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Up to {contingent_max} of Nvidia's guarantees cannot be tied to a named partner; CoreWeave, Firmus and SharonAI support may sit inside it.
relationships.definition: Nvidia guarantees leases, power contracts and hardware financing of partners and discloses the maximum it could have to pay. This record subtracts the guarantees whose beneficiary is named: the SB Energy guaranties for OpenAI's leases and the Nscale lease guarantee. What remains is guarantee exposure to partners Nvidia does not name, mostly the power and systems credit support first shown in November 2026.

contingent_max.label: analysis
contingent_max.note: Analysis. Maximum on both sides. Composition of the remainder: land, power and shell guarantees for unnamed neoclouds of $3.5B (ev_30026) less Nscale's $0.86B, plus power and systems credit support of $9.5B (ev_30025) whose partners Nvidia does not name.

components.note: Disclosed: total maximum gross exposure under guarantees at 2026-10-25
Less SB Energy credit support guarantees for OpenAI's PORTS-Pike leases (rel_openai_gu_2026)
Less Nscale Ward County lease guarantee (rel_nscale_gu_2025)

contingent_max.trigger: An unnamed Nvidia partner defaults on a facility lease, power or hardware financing obligation that Nvidia guarantees

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia pays only when the guaranteed partner defaults, so the exposure grows exactly as the partner weakens.
credit.tenor: Five to seven years for lease guarantees; power and systems terms not disclosed
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: An unnamed neocloud defaults on a guaranteed lease or hardware financing
first_order.mechanism: Unattributed guarantees convert into a payment by Nvidia net of escrow and recovery
first_order.text: A default by a partner Nvidia does not name would become an Nvidia payment with no prior warning to readers.

second_order.trigger: Lenders to unnamed neoclouds price loans on Nvidia's guarantee
second_order.mechanism: Unattributed credit support lowers partners' financing costs
second_order.text: Nvidia discloses $9.5 billion of power and systems credit support and $3.5 billion of land, power and shell guarantees for neoclouds without naming who benefits, so lenders' reliance on them cannot be traced.

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified: CoreWeave land, power and shell framework (rel_coreweave_gu_2026, framework only, no amount); Firmus credit support (rel_firmus_bk_2026, size not disclosed); SharonAI credit support model (rel_sharonai_bk_2026). Any of these could sit in the remainder, so it is an upper bound on what is truly unattributed. Nvidia had made no guarantee payments to date (ev_50045). The SB Energy cap is counted at its full $105B by Nvidia although no guaranty is effective until a building is ready for service in fiscal 2029; the subtraction uses the same basis. Basis check after the critic review: both subtractions are caps stated by a source (SB Energy line in Nvidia's own table; Nscale's 'up to' guarantee amount, which matches Nvidia's $860 million single partner figure).

relationships.title: Unattributed neocloud (AI cloud) agreements: capacity Nvidia agreed to buy back at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia stands behind up to {contingent_max} of neocloud capacity; SharonAI and Firmus are known partners, but no partner's share is disclosed.
relationships.definition: Neoclouds buy Nvidia systems and Nvidia commits to rent the resulting capacity for about six years; the neocloud sells the capacity to others first and Nvidia uses or pays for what is left. The commitments take effect only if the neocloud finances the purchase and Nvidia accepts the capacity. No named agreement has a disclosed Nvidia maximum; SharonAI (headline up to $4.88 billion) and Firmus are named but not quantified, so the whole disclosed maximum is shown as unattributed.

contingent_max.label: analysis
contingent_max.note: Analysis. Equal to Nvidia's disclosed maximum, which assumes the financing and acceptance contingencies are met. No named agreement has a disclosed Nvidia maximum, so nothing is subtracted. SharonAI's 'up to $4.88 billion' is its headline contract value and its 10-Q says the arrangement has no fixed aggregate value, so it is not a like for like maximum and was removed after the critic review.

components.note: Disclosed: neocloud agreements, maximum commitment at 2026-10-25

contingent_max.trigger: Neoclouds secure financing, deploy and Nvidia accepts the capacity, and the neoclouds then cannot sell it to third parties, so Nvidia must buy it

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia's payments grow when neoclouds fail to sell capacity to third parties, which is when those neoclouds are weakest.
credit.tenor: About six years, mostly fiscal 2028 to 2032 and after
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: AI compute demand softens and Unattributed neoclouds cannot sell capacity
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia buys the unsold capacity under the Unattributed neocloud agreements
first_order.text: If neoclouds cannot sell their capacity to others, Nvidia pays for what is left, so a demand slowdown turns sales to these partners into rental costs for Nvidia.

second_order.trigger: Unattributed neoclouds use the Nvidia agreement to raise debt to buy Nvidia systems
second_order.mechanism: Financing depends on the Nvidia commitment, which is itself conditional on financing
second_order.text: The commitments take effect only once a neocloud secures financing, so they help neoclouds raise the money they use to buy Nvidia systems (analysis).

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified (not subtracted): SharonAI (rel_sharonai_bk_2026; order of 2026-06-08, six years, five phases, revenue share; 8-K headline 'up to $4.88 billion' (ev_40144) while its 10-Q of 2026-11-16 says the arrangement does not specify a fixed aggregate contractual value (ev_40146)); CoreWeave (rel_coreweave_bk_2025; residual capacity order with an initial value of $6.3B, classification between this line and cloud service agreements not stated); Firmus (rel_firmus_bk_2026; revenue sharing and credit support model, size not disclosed); IREN (rel_iren_lb_2026) and Nscale (rel_nscale_lb_2025), whose rentals may sit here or in cloud service agreements (analysis). Classification: Nvidia describes these as agreements where the neocloud buys Nvidia infrastructure, Nvidia commits to rent the capacity for about six years, the neocloud can sell to third parties first and Nvidia shares revenue; the category appeared in Q2 FY2027 and its schedule shows nothing payable in the rest of FY2027. Value before the critic review: $27.12B with SharonAI subtracted. The aggregate was $36B at 2026-07-26 (ev_50079).

relationships.title: Unattributed multi-year cloud service agreements at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia has {committed_total} of cloud rental commitments; CoreWeave, IREN and Nscale are known providers, but no provider's remaining balance is disclosed.
relationships.definition: Nvidia rents cloud compute from cloud providers under multi-year agreements to support its research and development, and discloses the remaining commitment. No named rental has a disclosed remaining commitment at the same date: CoreWeave, IREN and Nscale give only an initial order value or total contract values. Nothing is subtracted, so the whole aggregate is shown as unattributed.

committed_total.label: analysis
committed_total.note: Analysis. Equal to the disclosed aggregate: no named rental has a stated remaining (unpaid) commitment at 2026-10-25, which is the like for like amount for this line. Removed after the critic review: CoreWeave $6.3B (the order form's initial value, not a commitment balance), IREN $3.4B and Nscale $1.2B (total contract values at signing; payments since are not disclosed). Upper bound on what is truly unattributed, since named rentals may sit inside it.

components.note: Disclosed: multi-year cloud service agreements, remaining commitment at 2026-10-25

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Rental commitments are fixed obligations; their burden rises with weaker AI demand but does not grow with a provider's distress.
credit.tenor: Up to six years; fiscal 2027 to 2032 and after
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: Nvidia's research need for rented compute falls
first_order.mechanism: Unattributed cloud service agreements still require payment unless reduced or terminated
first_order.text: Nvidia owed $28 billion under cloud service agreements at 25 October 2026 and does not say what it still owes each provider, so it keeps paying even if its own compute needs fall.

second_order.trigger: Providers in the Unattributed remainder bought Nvidia systems to serve these rentals
second_order.mechanism: Nvidia's rent becomes the provider's revenue, which services debt raised to buy Nvidia hardware
second_order.text: Providers Nvidia rents from gain contracted revenue they can borrow against to buy Nvidia systems; which providers hold the unnamed part is not disclosed (analysis).

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified (not subtracted): CoreWeave residual capacity order of 2025-09-09 (rel_coreweave_bk_2025; the 8-K gives an initial value of $6.3B, not a commitment balance, and neither side says the order sits in this aggregate), CoreWeave master services agreement order forms (rel_coreweave_lb_2023; payments only disclosed); IREN five-year cloud services contract (rel_iren_lb_2026; about $3.4B total contract value, signed May 2026, payments to date not disclosed); Nscale reserved GPU clusters (rel_nscale_lb_2025; aggregate amount $1.2B across order forms with 12 to 48 month terms from July 2025, payments to date not disclosed); hyperscaler rentals (rel_microsoft_cx_2025, rel_google_cx_2025 carry no amounts); Lambda (no amount in the register). Whether CoreWeave, IREN and Nscale sit in this line or in neocloud agreements is not stated by Nvidia (analysis). Values before the critic review: $17.1B with all three subtracted; $23.4B with CoreWeave removed. Aggregate was $29B at 2026-07-26 (ev_10030).

relationships.title: Unattributed equity investment commitments (unfunded) at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Up to {committed_total} of Nvidia's unfunded equity commitments cannot be tied to a named deal; unpaid OpenAI and Anthropic amounts may sit inside it.
relationships.definition: Nvidia has committed to make equity investments in frontier labs, infrastructure financiers and other private companies, subject to contingencies, and discloses the unfunded total. This record subtracts named commitments signed before 2026-10-25 and not yet paid. What remains is committed money for investees Nvidia does not name, and it is an upper bound because the unfunded parts of the OpenAI and Anthropic commitments are not disclosed.

committed_total.label: analysis
committed_total.note: Analysis. Nvidia counts commitments subject to contingencies, so named commitments signed before the date with a stated unfunded amount are subtracted: SB Energy's IPO private placement (about $1.5B, payable only if the IPO closes by 15 May 2027), NAVER ($1B signed 2026-07-24, closing pending) and the Nscale NVIDIA Sale ($1.0B, due to close around 2026-11-16). Upper bound: the unfunded parts of the OpenAI and Anthropic commitments are not disclosed.

components.note: Less SB Energy IPO concurrent private placement, about $1.5B unfunded, contingent on the IPO closing by 2027-05-15 (rel_sb_energy_eq_2026)
Less NAVER private placement, $1B signed 2026-07-24, precondition met 2026-10-27, closing pending (rel_naver_eq_2026)
Less Nscale NVIDIA Sale, a further $1.0B of notes or non-voting shares, closing about 2026-11-16 (rel_nscale_fc_2026)

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Commitments are paid as investees raise money; they move with the AI funding cycle but are fixed in size and do not grow with distress.
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: Contingencies on the Unattributed commitments are met
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia pays cash for equity in unnamed investees
first_order.text: Nvidia's $20 billion of unfunded equity commitments at 25 October 2026 fall mostly in fiscal 2028, when the cash goes to investees not all of whom are named.

second_order.trigger: Investees behind the Unattributed commitments rely on Nvidia money to buy compute
second_order.mechanism: Nvidia equity can return as purchases of Nvidia systems
second_order.text: Nvidia says these commitments focus on frontier labs and infrastructure financiers; without names, whether the money returns as Nvidia revenue cannot be tested.

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified: OpenAI Series C ($30B committed; funded and unfunded split not disclosed, rel_openai_eq_2026); Anthropic: November 2025 agreement up to $10B (rel_anthropic_eqc_2025) and the $10.0B IPO placement that closed 2026-11-20 (rel_anthropic_eq_2026); whether it was a commitment at 2026-10-25 is not disclosed (analysis: the commitment schedule shows only $5B for the rest of fiscal 2027). Firmus 2026 round (rel_firmus_eq_2026b, no amount); Helix and Brookfield LP interests (no amounts). Not commitments: IREN investment rights (no obligation to exercise), Meta and Wayve letters (headline only). Caveat: the Nscale NVIDIA Sale may settle in convertible notes, which are debt until the IPO; NAVER's precondition was met 2026-10-27, two days after the date. Aggregate was $25B at 2026-07-26 (ev_10032).

relationships.title: Unattributed supply and capacity commitments at 2026-10-25 (no prepayment aggregate disclosed)
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia has committed {committed_total} to suppliers it does not name, a fixed cost if demand for its systems slows.
relationships.definition: Nvidia has committed to buy components and manufacturing capacity from suppliers, mostly memory and wafers, and discloses the total. Named supply deals such as Amkor, KYEC and Corning cannot be subtracted: no source states an unpaid amount owed by Nvidia under any of them at the balance sheet date. The whole aggregate is therefore recorded as unattributed.

committed_total.label: analysis
committed_total.note: Analysis. Nothing could be attributed: Nvidia has not disclosed a prepaid supply balance since 2025-10-26, and named prepayment agreements cannot be split between paid (an asset) and unpaid (inside this commitment).

components.note: Disclosed: supply and capacity commitments at 2026-10-25

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the aggregate in Exhibits 99.2 and 99.3 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 for the quarter ended 2026-10-25 and names no counterparty within it.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No counterparty disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder; named items subtracted carry their own reconciliation in their records. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Supply commitments become a burden when AI demand falls, but they do not grow as any one supplier weakens; prepayments carry supplier delivery risk.
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total.

first_order.trigger: Demand for Nvidia systems falls below plan
first_order.mechanism: Unattributed supply commitments must still be paid or settled
first_order.text: Nvidia's supply and capacity commitments reached $390 billion at 25 October 2026, so a demand fall would leave it paying for components and capacity it cannot sell.

second_order.trigger: Suppliers expand capacity on the strength of the Unattributed commitments
second_order.mechanism: Supplier capital spending depends on Nvidia's orders
second_order.text: Named suppliers such as Amkor and KYEC are building capacity on Nvidia's advances, so a cut in Nvidia orders would leave unnamed suppliers with idle lines too (analysis).

relationships.notes: Named but not quantified against this aggregate: Amkor (rel_amkor_pp_2026; Nvidia says multiyear agreements total nearly $3 billion including prepayments, committed amount not attributable because Amkor does not name the customer); KYEC capacity reservation advance ($1.1B per Nvidia's release, paid part not stated, rel_kyec_pp_2026); Corning customer deposit (rel_corning_pp_2026; Corning does not name the customer, committed amount unknown); Ibiden, Unimicron and SPIL (no amounts). Paid parts sit in prepaid assets, which Nvidia stopped breaking out after 2025-10-26 (last disclosed: long-term $1,536M, ev_10147; short-term $2.0B, ev_10148). The aggregate was $279B at 2026-07-26 (ev_10029).

relationships.title: Unattributed data center leases not commenced at 2026-10-25
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia has signed {committed_total} of long data center leases on its own credit, some for capacity it may pass to other companies.
relationships.definition: Nvidia has signed data center leases with terms of up to twenty years that have not yet started, expected to commence between the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2033. Nvidia says it may assign some of these leases to third parties, so it has signed long leases on its own credit for capacity that others may use. Neither the landlords nor the third parties are named, so the whole amount is shown as unattributed.

committed_total.label: analysis
committed_total.note: Analysis. Equal to the disclosed total of data center leases not commenced; no named lease has a disclosed amount, so nothing is subtracted. Lease payments become due only as each lease commences (mostly fiscal 2032 and after).

components.note: Disclosed: data center leases not commenced at 2026-10-25

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia discloses the total in Exhibit 99.2 to its Form 8-K of 2026-11-17 and says it may assign some of these leases to third parties; it names no landlord or assignee.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: No landlord or assignee disclosure exists for an unattributed remainder. No disclosure found as of 2026-11-23.

credit.wwr_reason: Nvidia owes the rent whatever happens to the party it assigns capacity to until an assignment is completed; the burden rises with weaker AI demand, and if an intended assignee weakens before taking the lease Nvidia keeps paying.
credit.tenor: Up to twenty years; commencing Q4 fiscal 2027 to fiscal 2033
credit.notes: Analysis. Remainder computed in R7 at one balance sheet date, 2026-10-25; excluded from every total. Secondary type GU because leases signed for others to use work as credit support for them.

first_order.trigger: Nvidia cannot find third parties to take assignment of the leases
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia remains the tenant and pays rent on Unattributed data center leases for up to twenty years
first_order.text: If Nvidia cannot assign data center leases meant for others, it bears the rent on terms of up to twenty years for space it may not need.

second_order.trigger: Developers finance buildings on the strength of Nvidia as tenant
second_order.mechanism: Landlords of the Unattributed leases borrow against Nvidia's credit while the eventual user is a weaker company
second_order.text: Landlords of leases Nvidia signs and plans to reassign can finance buildings on Nvidia's credit, so capacity reaches tenants that could not sign such leases alone (analysis).

relationships.notes: At 2026-07-26 Nvidia's 10-Q split this commitment into data center leases not commenced of $25B (ev_10031) and a separate line, data center leases not commenced for third party, of $20B (ev_10037), with terms of about fifteen years that it expected to reassign to third parties (ev_190008); it warned that delays in completing assignments could leave it bearing the lease costs (ev_190009). The October disclosure gives one line of $74B, terms up to twenty years (ev_190006), commencement Q4 FY2027 to FY2033 (ev_190007), and says Nvidia may assign some of these leases to third parties (ev_190005); it no longer splits own use from third party. Analysis: the total rose by $29B in one quarter against the July sum of $45B. Named but not quantified: none; no landlord or assignee is named by Nvidia. Related: the SB Energy PORTS-Pike guaranties (rel_openai_gu_2026) are guarantees of OpenAI's leases, not Nvidia's own leases, and are not part of this line (analysis).
